name: NIS2 — Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on network and information systems security

sources.scope: Obligations applying to essential and important entities. NIS2 is a directive, so national transposition may add or tighten requirements — check the local implementing act and add items to this file where it goes further.
sources.crosswalk: Indicative mapping to NIST CSF 2.0, maintained in this file

levels.d: No evidence the outcome is addressed.
Documented, approved and applied across scope.
Measured, reviewed and enforced with evidence.
Continuously improved against metrics and threat change.

effort.M: Medium — project effort using existing tooling
effort.H: High — new capability, tooling or budget required

priority.d: More than 2.0 below the target maturity
At or above target — sustain the control

groups.name: Governance (Art. 20)
groups.desc: Management body approval, oversight, accountability and training obligations.

sections.name: Management body duties
sections.desc: Approval of measures, oversight of implementation, accountability and mandatory training.

controls.text: Art. 20.1 Management body approval and oversight

groups.name: Risk-management measures (Art. 21)
groups.desc: The ten minimum measures of Article 21(2), the proportionality requirement and the supply chain provisions of Article 21(3).

sections.name: Risk analysis and security policy — 21(2)(a)
sections.desc: All-hazards approach, risk analysis methodology and the information system security policy.

sections.name: Incident handling — 21(2)(b)
sections.desc: Incident handling process and the detection and logging capability behind it.

sections.name: Continuity and crisis management — 21(2)(c)
sections.desc: Business continuity, backup management, disaster recovery and crisis management.

sections.name: Supply chain security — 21(2)(d) and 21(3)
sections.desc: Supplier assurance, contractual security requirements and supplier-specific vulnerability assessment.

sections.name: Acquisition, development and vulnerability handling — 21(2)(e)
sections.desc: Security in system acquisition, development and maintenance, and vulnerability handling and disclosure.

controls.text: Art. 21.2e.1 Security in acquisition and development

sections.name: Effectiveness assessment — 21(2)(f)
sections.desc: Assessing whether the risk-management measures actually work.

sections.name: Cyber hygiene and training — 21(2)(g)
sections.desc: Basic cyber hygiene practices and cybersecurity training.

sections.name: Cryptography — 21(2)(h)
sections.desc: Policies and procedures on the use of cryptography and encryption.

sections.name: HR security, access control and asset management — 21(2)(i)
sections.desc: Human resources security, access control policy and asset management.

sections.name: Authentication and secured communications — 21(2)(j)
sections.desc: Multi-factor or continuous authentication and secured voice, video, text and emergency communications.

sections.name: Corrective measures — 21(4)
sections.desc: Correcting identified non-compliance without undue delay.

groups.name: Incident reporting (Art. 23)
groups.desc: Determination of significance, notification of recipients, and the 24-hour, 72-hour, intermediate and one-month reporting timeline.

sections.name: Significance and recipient notification
sections.desc: Assessing incident significance and notifying service recipients and, where appropriate, of significant cyber threats.

sections.name: Reporting timeline
sections.desc: Early warning, incident notification, intermediate report, final report and progress report.

groups.name: Wider obligations (Art. 3, 24, 25, 29, 32)
groups.desc: Registration, certification, standards, information sharing and readiness for supervision.

sections.name: Registration, certification and standards
sections.desc: Entity registration and information currency, use of certification schemes and recognised standards.

sections.name: Information sharing and supervision
sections.desc: Participation in information-sharing arrangements and the ability to demonstrate compliance to the supervisor.

references.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
references.note: Indicative crosswalk to NIST CSF 2.0, so NIS2 findings can also be reported against a technical control framework. It is not an official mapping. Purely regulatory obligations such as registration and reporting deadlines have no meaningful CSF counterpart and are left unmapped.

items.q: Do the management bodies approve the cybersecurity risk-management measures, oversee their implementation, and accept accountability for non-compliance?
items.rec: Record management body approval of the risk-management measures and minute ongoing oversight. Under NIS2 the management body can be held personally liable, so the evidence trail matters as much as the measures.

items.q: Do management body members follow training to gain sufficient knowledge and skills to identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices, and is similar training offered to employees?
items.rec: Deliver and record cybersecurity training for management body members specific to the entity's risk profile, and offer equivalent training to staff on a regular basis.

items.q: Are appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures in place to manage risks to network and information systems, following an all-hazards approach?
items.rec: Document the all-hazards risk-management approach and justify proportionality against entity size, exposure, likelihood and societal impact, so supervisory challenge can be answered.

items.q: Are policies on risk analysis in place, with a documented and repeatable risk assessment methodology?
items.rec: Adopt a documented risk assessment methodology with defined criteria and scales, applied consistently and producing comparable results.

items.q: Is an approved information system security policy in place, communicated, and reviewed at planned intervals?
items.rec: Maintain an approved information system security policy set with a named owner, review cycle and evidence of communication and enforcement.

items.q: Is an incident handling process established covering prevention, detection, analysis, containment, response and recovery?
items.rec: Establish and exercise a documented incident handling process covering the full lifecycle, with roles, severity criteria and escalation defined.

items.q: Are incidents detected and logged, with sufficient information retained to support analysis and regulatory reporting?
items.rec: Deploy central log collection and correlation sufficient to detect incidents and to evidence the timeline required for NIS2 reporting.

items.q: Are business continuity arrangements in place, including plans for maintaining or restoring operations after a disruptive incident?
items.rec: Maintain business continuity plans derived from a current business impact analysis, with defined recovery objectives and named activation authority.

items.q: Are backups managed, protected against tampering, and restore-tested on a defined cycle?
items.rec: Maintain immutable or offline backups with a documented restore-testing cycle including at least one full system recovery test per year.

items.q: Are disaster recovery arrangements documented and tested against defined recovery time and recovery point objectives?
items.rec: Test disaster recovery end to end at least annually so that stated recovery objectives are evidenced rather than assumed.

items.q: Are crisis management arrangements in place, including decision authority, escalation and internal and external communication?
items.rec: Establish a crisis management structure with named roles, escalation thresholds and pre-approved communication templates, and rehearse it.

items.q: Are security-related aspects of relationships with direct suppliers and service providers assessed and managed?
items.rec: Establish supplier security assurance covering identification, risk-based due diligence and ongoing monitoring of direct suppliers and service providers.

items.q: Are security requirements agreed contractually with suppliers, including incident notification obligations?
items.rec: Apply a standard contractual security schedule to suppliers, including incident notification timelines that allow the entity to meet its own NIS2 reporting deadlines.

items.q: Does supplier risk assessment take into account the vulnerabilities specific to each direct supplier, the overall quality of their products and their cybersecurity practices, including secure development procedures?
items.rec: Assess each critical supplier individually rather than by category, covering their known vulnerabilities, product quality and secure development practices.

items.q: Is security addressed in the acquisition, development and maintenance of network and information systems?
items.rec: Define security requirements and a security gate for acquisition, development and maintenance activity, explicitly covering low-code and citizen development.

items.q: Are vulnerabilities handled and disclosed through a defined process, including a route for external parties to report them?
items.rec: Operate risk-based vulnerability management with remediation SLAs, and publish a vulnerability disclosure policy with a monitored security contact.

items.q: Are policies and procedures in place to assess the effectiveness of the cybersecurity risk-management measures?
items.rec: Define measures of control effectiveness, assess them on a fixed cycle through audit, testing or metrics, and report the results to the management body.

items.q: Are basic cyber hygiene practices implemented, including patching, secure configuration, account management and malware protection?
items.rec: Implement and evidence the cyber hygiene baseline — patching to SLA, hardened configuration baselines, least-privilege account management and managed malware protection.

items.q: Is cybersecurity training provided to staff, appropriate to their role, and is completion tracked?
items.rec: Deliver induction and annual refresher training to all staff with role-relevant content for privileged and technical roles, and track completion.

items.q: Are policies and procedures in place regarding the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption?
items.rec: Maintain a cryptography policy covering approved algorithms and protocol versions, key lifecycle management, and encryption of data at rest and in transit.

items.q: Is security addressed across the employment lifecycle, including screening, terms of employment and termination?
items.rec: Embed security in the HR lifecycle: proportionate screening, security obligations in contracts, and evidenced, timely access removal on exit or role change.

items.q: Is an access control policy in place, applying least privilege, with access rights reviewed and revoked when no longer required?
items.rec: Maintain an access control policy applying least privilege, with a documented recertification cycle covering privileged and business application access.

items.q: Are assets identified, inventoried, classified and managed through their lifecycle?
items.rec: Maintain a complete asset inventory with named owners covering hardware, software, cloud services and data, reconciled on a defined cycle.

items.q: Are multi-factor or continuous authentication solutions used where appropriate?
items.rec: Enforce multi-factor authentication for all remote, administrative and cloud access, removing legacy authentication bypass paths.

items.q: Are secured voice, video and text communications used where appropriate?
items.rec: Use secured communication platforms for sensitive business communication, with encryption in transit and controlled external sharing.

items.q: Are secured emergency communication systems in place for use when primary systems are unavailable?
items.rec: Provide and test an out-of-band emergency communication channel, independent of corporate identity and network, for use during a major incident.

items.q: Where measures are found not to comply, are corrective measures taken without undue delay?
items.rec: Track identified non-compliance in a corrective action register with owner, deadline and evidence of effectiveness review.

items.q: Are incidents assessed against the significance criteria — severe operational disruption or financial loss, or considerable material or non-material damage to others?
items.rec: Embed the NIS2 significance criteria in the incident record so that the decision to report is a documented assessment rather than a judgement call under pressure.

items.q: Are recipients of services notified without undue delay of significant incidents likely to adversely affect the provision of those services?
items.rec: Define the trigger, timeline and route for notifying service recipients, with pre-approved content, and rehearse it.

items.q: Where appropriate, are recipients notified of significant cyber threats and of any measures or remedies they can take in response?
items.rec: Establish the route and criteria for notifying recipients of significant cyber threats, including the remedies available to them.

items.q: Is an early warning submitted to the CSIRT or competent authority without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of a significant incident?
items.rec: Build the 24-hour early warning into the incident process with an automated reminder and an out-of-hours route, and confirm who is authorised to submit.

items.q: Is an incident notification submitted within 72 hours, updating the early warning and providing an initial assessment including severity, impact and indicators of compromise?
items.rec: Prepare a 72-hour notification template covering severity, impact and indicators of compromise, and rehearse producing it from the available evidence.

items.q: Is an intermediate report provided on the request of the CSIRT or competent authority, with relevant status updates?
items.rec: Assign ownership for responding to intermediate report requests during an incident, so supervisory requests do not compete with response work.

items.q: Is a final report submitted within one month of the incident notification, covering detailed description, severity, threat type, root cause, mitigation and cross-border impact?
items.rec: Build the one-month final report into the post-incident review so root cause, mitigation and cross-border impact are produced once and serve both purposes.

items.q: Where the incident is ongoing at the time of the final report deadline, is a progress report submitted and a final report provided within one month of handling the incident?
items.rec: Track the progress report obligation for incidents that remain ongoing past one month, so the final report deadline is managed rather than missed.

items.q: Has the entity registered with the competent authority and does it keep its submitted information — name, address, sector, contact details, IP ranges and Member States of operation — up to date?
items.rec: Confirm registration is complete and assign ownership for keeping the submitted entity information current, notifying changes without undue delay.

items.q: Where required or chosen, are European cybersecurity certification schemes used to demonstrate compliance with particular requirements?
items.rec: Assess whether relevant European certification schemes apply, and document the decision either way so the position is defensible at supervision.

items.q: Is the use of relevant European and international standards and technical specifications considered in implementing the risk-management measures?
items.rec: Anchor the control set to a recognised standard such as ISO/IEC 27001 or the NIST CSF, and document the mapping to the Article 21(2) measures.

items.q: Where the entity participates in information-sharing arrangements, are they operated within trusted communities with appropriate protection for the information shared?
items.rec: Where participating in information-sharing arrangements, document the community, the protections applied and any notification obligation to the competent authority.

items.q: Is the entity able to demonstrate compliance on request, providing evidence, policies, audit results and access for on-site inspection or off-site supervision?
items.rec: Maintain a supervision-ready evidence pack — policies, risk assessment, register of measures, audit and test results, incident records — so a supervisory request does not become a project.
